description.narrative:
The project seeks to address a number of issues around integral human development through the Justice, Development and Peace structures of the Catholic Church in Nigeria, with a special focus on Kogi State in Central Nigeria. Internal governance systems in most communities in Nigeria are weak, leading to an inability of the community members to demand for and positively engage their local and state governments for improved provision of social infrastructure and services. There is a low level of awareness of the laws and statutes that exist to regulate the operations public offices and departments, making it difficult for the people to identify lapses in governance. In some cases, existing legislation is weak or absent, creating an open space for abuse of the authority of public office, and allowing corruption and mediocrity to thrive. Although the problem of underdevelopment is multi-factorial, one contributory factor is the lack of strong community governance structures that can work together with the local and state governments to serve the common good. The weak community governance processes results from absent or weak community development committees (CDCs) and low awareness of the citizenry on their rights and responsibilities. Many existing CDCs do not meet regularly; some are ignorant of due process and regulatory frameworks for public governance. The relevance of the CDCs is equally stalled by the existence of individual and group interests that are served by the status quo. There is also a lack of transparency on the part of the government agencies, this hinders citizens from monitoring government activities and permits corruption to thrive. Government agencies exhibit poor understanding and sensitivity to community needs, often as a result of weak interface with community actors.
Project Outcomes include: 1. The Church and citizens influence national level policy in Nigeria. 2. Citizen’s participation in governance is enhanced in four local government areas (LGAs) in Kogi State; 3. Community development influenced by citizens in targeted areas.
The main strategy adopted by the project will be to build the capacity of the Diocesan JDPC staff and selected community advocates to engage the government in dialogue around improved civic participation in governance. This will include increased participation of the citizenry in planning and budgeting for development and monitoring and evaluation of the activities of the various government agencies in the state. To achieve this, CCFN and partners will carry out workshops on advocacy, governance processes, budget monitoring, and gender-relevant laws and policies. Beneficiaries of these workshops, in addition to the diocesan JDPC, will include representatives of key stakeholder groups, community and religious leaders, and influential Catholics who have sufficient clout to champion advocacy initiatives. The project will also support participating communities to engage their local governments in regular discussion on the prioritization, commissioning, and monitoring of development projects in their communities.
